agents.reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established four things I had wrong: (a) my exit P/E mixed EME (with EPS not on the cited page) into a revenue-weighted median; on the whole-company median (MTZ 16.6, PWR 35.2, PRIM 17.1, MYRG 20.2 = 18.65x) and DY's own 12.13x, k = 0.8 gives 13.2x (revenue-weighting with the corrected Building Systems peers gives the same 18.62x). (b) Supplier finance does not bear interest, so I moved it out of net debt; my own AP-days test against the four pre-program quarters (18.40 days vs 27.67 now) makes 204.3 debt-like, an equity adjustment. (c) I counted SBC twice; shares now fall only by buybacks (-0.9%/yr). (d) My EV/EBITDA leg's growth division was ad hoc; it now reads LTM GAAP EBITDA like the peers' trailing figures (exit 10.9x on my own EBITDA TTM 906.8), at weight 0.3 because only two peers carry it. I also fixed the interest rate (6.1% on net debt, not 5.4% of gross debt) and the Street NTM EPS in the thesis break (18.23, not 19.8). The approved drivers are unchanged; base value $313.87 (P/E $301.06, EV/EBITDA $343.75). Base rates (my lane) still shape the tails: the FY2019 analog (guide cut, -62% over 13 months, P/E trough ~10x), MasTec's Q3 2026 Communications cut and AT&T's 2027-28 capex trim (-4%) argue my central backlog view sits below the approved path (about -3% of value, for Kilian), and set the downside at backlog -12%, margins -2/-3pt, multiples -2.5 turns ($145.76). Verizon held 2026 capex at $16-16.5B, so not every carrier is cutting. Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20%. The upside ($493.67) stays below the peer median multiple. Horizon NTM EPS from the build, 23.3, is +8% over the Street (~21.5) because the approved drivers follow DY's beat record; the research target (12m) is +42% on a stock that fell 61%, which base rates say should be read with the caution that today's price beats every blend as a forecast. 1-month: Q3 print Nov 18-25 inside the window; ladder unchanged, near neutral.
